assertions.name: zD_minus_bar_zD_is_exactly_h
assertions.source: sympy simplifies z_D - bar(z_D) - h to exactly 0; numerically the residual is < 1e-45 at both anchors (proton 4.52784e-72). This is the identity that makes the D-frame anomaly a closed form rather than a measured number.

assertions.name: alphaD_bar_anomaly_equals_h_squared_over_two
assertions.source: bar(alpha_D) + alpha_D - h^2/2 simplifies to 0 symbolically and is < 1e-45 at both anchors -- the closed form of the anomaly the eigenphase probe measured.

assertions.name: C_is_bar_odd_and_projected_D_is_bar_odd_but_raw_D_is_not
assertions.source: z_C is exactly bar-fixed and alpha_C exactly bar-odd; the projected D phase (alpha_D - h^2/4) is exactly bar-odd; the RAW D phase is not (its bar-sum is h^2/2 != 0). The three together are the iff of phaseTwice_bar_odd_iff_z_bar_fixed instantiated at both conventions.

assertions.name: bar_exchanges_the_two_loop_values_under_D_but_not_under_C
assertions.source: bar(z_D) - (z_D - h) simplifies to exactly 0: under D the bar involution sends z to the NEGATIVE-stabilisation loop value, which is what mirror must do since mirroring exchanges positive and negative crossings. Under C the same difference is exactly h (0.2090603 at the proton anchor): C's z is bar-FIXED, i.e. mirror-blind. This reverses the naive reading -- the h^2/2 phase anomaly is not a defect of D, it is the signature that D tracks the crossing-sign exchange while the phase FORMULA, written in the bar-fixed C frame, was carried over unchanged.

assertions.name: projection_is_the_phase_at_the_mean_loop_value_not_a_shift
assertions.source: alpha_D - h^2/4 = ((z_D + (z_D - h))/2 - 1)*h/2 exactly -- the SAME formula with the positive-stabilisation loop value replaced by the mean of the two. So the projection is not an ad-hoc shift but a re-derivation of the phase in the mirror-symmetric loop value, and under D the loop-mean and the bar-mean coincide (QOU.QBeta.zD_bar_mean_eq_loop_mean). Lean: QOU.QBeta.phaseTwice_projected_eq_loopMean.

description: Closed form for the Q_beta ladder phase's bar-anomaly, backing the numerically-measured D-frame projection. For alpha = (z-1)h/2 with h bar-odd, bar(alpha)+alpha = h*(z - bar z)/2 for ANY z, so the phase is mirror-covariant iff z is exactly bar-fixed (QOU.QBeta.phaseTwice_bar_odd_iff_z_bar_fixed, sorry-free). Convention C's z = sqrt(q)/(1+q) IS bar-fixed (corpus lemma z_bar_invariant_field, PR #3449) so alpha_C is bar-odd by structure. Convention D's z = q^3/(q^2+1) is not, and its anomaly is EXACTLY h: z_D - bar(z_D) = q - 1/q, symbolically and at both anchors. Hence bar(alpha_D)+alpha_D = h^2/2 and the projection alpha_D - h^2/4 is the UNIQUE mirror-covariant part -- forced, not fitted (QOU.QBeta.phaseTwiceD_sub_hsq_bar_odd). Sec.4 sharpens what the anomaly IS: bar(z_D) = z_D - h is the NEGATIVE-stabilisation loop value, so under D bar EXCHANGES the two Markov loop values -- exactly what mirror must do, since mirroring exchanges positive and negative crossings -- while C's bar-fixed z is mirror-BLIND and misses the exchange by h. The h^2/2 anomaly is therefore not a defect of D but the signature that D tracks the crossing-sign exchange while the phase FORMULA was carried over unchanged from the C frame. And the projection is not a shift: alpha_D - h^2/4 is the same formula at the MEAN of the two loop values, which under D equals the bar-mean (phaseTwice_projected_eq_loopMean, zD_bar_mean_eq_loop_mean). Motivation for using bar-parity as the test: the Ocneanu trace needs a writhe-dependent framing prefactor (Jones 1987 Sec. 5) and writhe is mirror-odd (WritheMarkovInvariance.writhe_inv), so a framing phase must be bar-odd. SCOPE: closes nothing. The projected D phase still leaves a residual ~42x the C-frame one; that residual is untouched and the standing fence against hunting further phase corrections holds. No value wired, no tier moved, D stays canonical.
